subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure wind speed?
questions.explain: An anemometer's rotating cups spin faster in stronger winds, giving the wind speed.

questions.q: In which units is atmospheric (air) pressure measured?
questions.explain: Air pressure is recorded in millibars (mb), typically around 1013 mb at sea level.

questions.q: Cloud cover is measured in which units?
questions.explain: Cloud cover is measured in oktas, or eighths of the sky covered by cloud.

questions.q: Why is a Stevenson screen painted white?
options: To reflect sunlight so the thermometers record the true air temperature
To absorb heat and warm the instruments inside
To make it easier for observers to see at night
To stop rain from entering the screen
questions.explain: The white surface reflects solar radiation, preventing the screen heating up and giving false temperature readings.

questions.q: Which instrument measures the humidity of the air?
questions.explain: A hygrometer measures humidity, the amount of water vapour in the air.

questions.q: In the northern hemisphere, why does the door of a Stevenson screen face north?
options: So direct sunlight does not fall on the thermometers when readings are taken
So the wind blows directly onto the instruments
So rain can drain away from the screen
So the screen receives the maximum amount of sunshine
questions.explain: A north-facing door keeps the sun off the thermometers when the observer opens it, avoiding inaccurate readings.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure precipitation, and in which units?
questions.explain: A rain gauge collects rainfall, which is measured in millimetres (mm).

questions.q: A depression is best described as an area of:
questions.explain: A depression is a system of low pressure that brings unsettled, wet and windy weather.

questions.q: An anticyclone is a system of:
questions.explain: An anticyclone is an area of high pressure, generally bringing settled, dry weather.

questions.q: In the northern hemisphere, in which direction do winds blow around the centre of a depression?
questions.explain: Around a northern-hemisphere depression winds blow anticlockwise, spiralling in towards the low-pressure centre.

questions.q: What type of weather is typically brought by the passing of a warm front?
options: Steady, prolonged rain from layered cloud
A short, heavy downpour then rapid clearing
Clear skies and severe overnight frost
Thick fog with no cloud above
questions.explain: A warm front rises gently, producing layered stratus-type cloud and long periods of steady rain.

questions.q: Why do anticyclones usually bring dry, cloudless weather?
options: Air descends, warms and suppresses cloud formation
Air rises rapidly, cools and condenses into cloud
Warm and cold fronts meet at the centre
Isobars are very close together, causing storms
questions.explain: In an anticyclone air sinks and warms, so water vapour does not condense and skies stay clear.

questions.q: On a synoptic chart the isobars are drawn very close together. What does this tell you about the weather?
questions.explain: Closely spaced isobars show a steep pressure gradient, which produces strong winds.

questions.q: What forms when a cold front catches up with the warm front ahead of it in a depression?
questions.explain: The faster-moving cold front lifts the warm air off the ground, creating an occluded front.

questions.q: A summer anticyclone becomes established over Northern Ireland. What weather is most likely?
options: Cold air with overnight frost and fog
questions.explain: In summer the sinking air of an anticyclone gives long, hot, dry and sunny days.

questions.q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide is a key greenhouse gas that traps outgoing heat in the atmosphere.

questions.q: A country wants to reduce the carbon dioxide it adds to the atmosphere. Which action would help most?
options: Generating electricity from renewable sources such as wind and solar
Clearing large areas of forest for farmland
Encouraging greater use of petrol cars
questions.explain: Renewable energy produces little or no CO2, unlike burning fossil fuels which is the main human source.

questions.q: Which of the following is a NATURAL cause of climate change?
options: Major volcanic eruptions releasing ash and gases
Burning of coal, oil and gas
questions.explain: Volcanic activity is a natural cause, while burning fuels, deforestation and traffic are human causes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a likely impact of global warming?
options: Growth of the polar ice caps
A decrease in extreme weather events
questions.explain: Warming melts ice and expands sea water, raising sea levels and threatening low-lying coasts.

questions.q: A low-lying island nation is worried about the effects of climate change. Which impact is the greatest threat to it?
options: Flooding of land due to rising sea levels
A permanent fall in average temperatures
An expansion of its total land area
questions.explain: Rising sea levels caused by melting ice and thermal expansion put low-lying islands at risk of flooding.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Geography (2017) specification; Our Changing Weather & Climate
